content.thinking: Found the bug: categorise passes title words without lowercasing, but the training pipeline lowercased everything, so v2 wasn't matching correctly. The fix is to lowercase words in categorise before passing to the model, which is safe for v1 too since it already lowercases. I'll add a test case with mixed-case input like "Kettle in brushed steel" to catch this, since existing tests happened to pass because their words were already lowercase.

Found it: `categorise()` in `categorising.py` forwards words without lowercasing, which V1 handled internally but V2 moved into its training pipeline—so under V2, capitalized words like "Kettle" miss the vocabulary and fall back to "General" with no confidence, matching the symptoms exactly.

input.explanation:
The fault, in src/io_shop/categorising.py as it stands on main: `categorise()` hands the model `title.split()` with the words' case unchanged. `CategoriserModel.predict` lowercases a word only when `lowercases_its_input` is true. V1 sets that to true; V2 sets it to false. The comment above V2 gives the reason: its training pipeline lowercases every title before building the vocabulary, so the model expects lowercase input. In this module nothing lowercases the words before they reach the model. Under V2, any capitalised word ("Kettle", "Wireless", "KEYBOARD") misses the lowercase vocabulary and the purchase is filed under "General" with confident=False. Nothing raises an error and nothing slows down. That is consistent with what the investigation reported: confidence dropped from about 0.90 to about 0.40 while errors and latency stayed flat after deploy/values-production.yaml switched `categoriser.model` from v1 to v2.

A caveat on which code this is about: everything above describes main. Revision 7c3ca00c7528df68d533f6e87acd4f23a55ab342 was deployed from another branch, and I have not read its copy of this file. The investigation says that revision's diff changed only deploy/values-production.yaml, which suggests its categorising.py matches main's, but I have not checked that.

The fix: `categorise()` now lowercases each word before passing it to the model, so the shop matches what V2's training pipeline does. V1 already lowercases inside `predict`, so V1 results should not change. Under V2, capitalised titles now look up the same lowercase keys the vocabulary was built from. The config can stay on v2 or be rolled back to v1. In this repository the only callers of `categorise` are the tests in tests/io_shop/test_categorising.py.

The tests: I added cases to tests/io_shop/test_categorising.py that categorise capitalised titles ("Kettle in brushed steel", "KEYBOARD with backlight", "Fitness Smartwatch") under V2 and assert a confident, correct category. They also assert that every model files the same capitalised title identically. These tests are written to fail against main's current `categorise` and pass with this change. I have not run them.

files.content:
"""Filing a purchase under a category - what the monthly statement's breakdown reads.

A purchase reaches the shop as the title the shopper saw and nothing else, and a
model decides which aisle it belongs in. Most titles name the thing outright -
a kettle, a backpack, a novel - so the model is a vocabulary rather than anything
cleverer: a title is split into words, and the first word the model knows says
where the purchase goes. A title it knows no word of is filed under "General",
which is where a shop's own catalogue puts anything it has not classified, and
the filing says the model was not confident of it.

That last part is the figure worth watching. A purchase filed under "General" is
not an error - nothing fails, the page renders, the shopper is charged what they
were charged - so the only sign a model has stopped recognising the catalogue is
how much of it it is still confident about.

Which model files a purchase arrives here already decided, the way every other
choice the deployment makes does. The versions live in this module; which one the
shop loads is the deployment's business - see `categoriser.model` in
`deploy/values-production.yaml`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Final

# Where a purchase goes when the model recognises nothing in its title - the
# catalogue's own name for unclassified, and the default a `Purchase` carries.
UNCATEGORISED: Final = "General"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Categorisation:
    """Where one purchase was filed, and whether the model knew why."""

    category: str
    confident: bool


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CategoriserModel:
    """One trained version of the categoriser.

    `vocabulary` maps a word to the category it files a purchase under, spelled as
    the model was trained on it. `lowercases_its_input` is whether the model folds
    the case of the words it is handed before looking them up, or takes them
    exactly as given.
    """

    version: str
    vocabulary: Mapping[str, str]
    lowercases_its_input: bool

    def predict(self, words: Sequence[str]) -> Categorisation:
        """The category of the first word this model knows, or `UNCATEGORISED`
        with no confidence when it knows none of them."""
        for word in words:
            looked_up = word.lower() if self.lowercases_its_input else word
            category = self.vocabulary.get(looked_up)

            if category is not None:
                return Categorisation(category=category, confident=True)

        return Categorisation(category=UNCATEGORISED, confident=False)


_THE_FIRST_VOCABULARY: Final[Mapping[str, str]] = {
    "headphones": "Audio",
    "speaker": "Audio",
    "keyboard": "Computing",
    "monitor": "Computing",
    "mouse": "Computing",
    "kettle": "Kitchen",
    "toaster": "Kitchen",
    "blender": "Kitchen",
    "lamp": "Home",
    "blanket": "Home",
    "backpack": "Travel",
    "suitcase": "Travel",
    "jacket": "Clothing",
    "trainers": "Clothing",
    "novel": "Books",
    "cookbook": "Books",
    "charger": "Accessories",
    "cable": "Accessories",
}

# The first model the shop ran. It folds case itself, so whatever reaches it is
# matched however the title happened to be capitalised.
V1: Final = CategoriserModel(
    version="v1",
    vocabulary=_THE_FIRST_VOCABULARY,
    lowercases_its_input=True,
)

# The upgrade, retrained on a catalogue that had grown two product lines since the
# first. Its tokeniser moved out of the model and into the training pipeline,
# which lowercases every title before the vocabulary is built - so the model now
# takes words exactly as it is given them, and is smaller and quicker for it.
V2: Final = CategoriserModel(
    version="v2",
    vocabulary={
        **_THE_FIRST_VOCABULARY,
        "smartwatch": "Wearables",
        "earbuds": "Audio",
    },
    lowercases_its_input=False,
)

# Every version the shop can load, by the name the deployment selects it with.
MODELS: Final[Mapping[str, CategoriserModel]] = {
    model.version: model for model in (V1, V2)
}


def categorise(title: str, model: CategoriserModel) -> Categorisation:
    """Where `model` files a purchase with this title.

    Words are lowercased here, before any model sees them, the way the training
    pipeline lowercased every title the vocabularies were built from. A model that
    no longer folds case itself (v2) would otherwise miss every capitalised word
    and file the purchase under `UNCATEGORISED` without a single error to show it.
    """
    return model.predict([word.lower() for word in title.split()])

input.summary: Lowercase title words before categorising so v2 (which does not fold case itself) recognises capitalised titles
